setup_summary.text: FY26 (July year-end) revenue was $11.48B, up 24.5%. GAAP operating income was $695M (6.1% margin vs 13.5%), net income $307M and diluted EPS $0.40 vs $1.60. Reported results include Chronosphere (closed Jan 29, 2026) and CyberArk/Idira (closed Feb 11, 2026). GAAP results also carry higher intangible amortization ($640M vs $166M), higher share-based compensation ($1.815B vs $1.300B) and a $620M fair-value loss on the CyberArk 2030 notes.

Q4 FY26 revenue was $3.41B, up 34%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.02, $0.04 above the top of the guided range, and management said it beat guidance on every metric. Derived Q4 GAAP operating margin was 5.0% and the derived GAAP net loss was $282M, against a 29.6% non-GAAP operating margin.

NGS ARR ended FY26 at $9.1B, up 63%, with nearly $1B of net new ARR in Q4. That included a nine-figure benefit from one large LLM customer migrating to Chronosphere. RPO was a record $21.2B, up 34%. Management reports about 22 net new platformizations in Q4 and net revenue retention above 120% for the platformized cohort.

The bar for the fiscal Q1 2027 print (consensus date per Finnhub: 2026-11-12, unconfirmed) is above guidance. Guidance is revenue $3.30-3.31B and non-GAAP EPS $0.96-0.98. Consensus is revenue $3.37B (about 1.8% above the top of the guide) and EPS $0.99. Consensus growth of about 36% compares with 33-34% guided.

Reported growth overstates organic growth. CyberArk and Chronosphere together added $930M of revenue and an $797M operating loss in FY26. Unaudited pro forma revenue growth was about 17% ($12.31B vs $10.49B), against 24% reported. The FY27 NGS ARR guide of 22-23% growth compares with 63% at year-end as the acquisitions lap.

Cash generation is strong. FY26 operating cash flow was $4.55B and GAAP-basis free cash flow was $4.11B; management's adjusted FCF was $4.41B (38.4% margin). FY27 is guided to a 38% adjusted FCF margin and FY28 to a 40% target. Cash and investments fell to $7.9B after $4.7B of net acquisition cash and $1.0B of buybacks.

Stock going into the print: PANW closed at $390.54 on Oct 27, slid about 3% intraday on Oct 29 (Fortinet-led sector selloff) and fell a further 4.12% on Oct 30. Coverage cites 80-90x forward earnings. Historical reaction is an average closing move of ±5.1% over the last 8 reports. No options-implied move is available.

view.text: No FY27 or Q1 gross margin guide exists. Management expects cloud hosting costs to grow faster than revenue and memory/storage cost pressure to persist; hardware is about 10% of revenue. This is my estimate, not guidance; SBC is the swing factor (about $140M per point of revenue).

since_filing.text: Estimates have not moved: a Zacks-sourced article dated Oct 27 says consensus estimates for PANW's FY27 and FY28 earnings were unchanged over the past 30 days. A Barchart preview dated Oct 28 reports 40 of 56 analysts at Strong Buy and an average price target of $402.10. It says PANW beat consensus in three of the last four quarters and missed once. The beat sizes and the basis (GAAP or non-GAAP) are not given, and its $0.52 EPS figure does not match PANW's reported figures.

Peer read-through is mixed. Fortinet's Oct 29 Q3 showed revenue +20%, product revenue +37% and billings +29% (supportive of firewall demand), but the stock fell about 20% intraday on a lowered full-year service revenue forecast. PANW fell 3.2% to about $381.86 and CrowdStrike 1.6% intraday in sympathy. Commentary argues security stocks are not being rewarded for beats.

PANW fell a further 4.12% on Oct 30 after closing at $390.54 on Oct 27. Coverage cites 80-90x forward earnings and flags the deceleration in NGS ARR growth from 63% to 22-23% as a downside risk into the print.

New PAN-OS security headlines inside the window: on Oct 20, The Register reported multiple ransomware groups exploiting authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect since early June. On Oct 28 PANW confirmed active exploitation of 'PHP2Shell' vulnerabilities against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, with hotfixes rolling out through Oct 30. A campaign analysis on Oct 31 cites 25 compromised systems. The 10-K already disclosed a May 2026 authentication bypass; whether it is the same flaw as CVE-2026-0257 is unconfirmed.

Corporate items: on Oct 30 PANW recommended stockholders reject an unsolicited mini-tender offer from Tutanota LLC at $450 per share for up to 250,000 shares (about 0.03% of the stock). The Oct 27 proxy cites an Oct 9 close of $418.78 and, in a footnote, says FY26 earnings included fair-value changes on the CyberArk convertible notes and capped calls. I found no PANW buyback announcement since the 10-K; the $1.2B buyback headline of Oct 29-30 is Fortinet's.

Zscaler, the main SASE competitor, rose 19% in the 30 days to Oct 26 on the AI-security narrative. Its fiscal Q1 2027 guide is revenue of $935-939M with roughly 17% implied ARR growth. That compares loosely with PANW's FY27 NGS ARR growth guide of 22-23% (different metrics).

key_debates.question: Can PANW clear a consensus bar that sits above its own guide, in a tape that has stopped rewarding beats?

bull.text: Management says it builds guidance from consensus, pipeline and territory plans and expects to exceed consensus. In Q4 it beat the top of its EPS guide by $0.04 and exceeded guidance on every metric. Bookings accelerated for a second straight quarter on a pro forma basis.

bear.text: Consensus revenue ($3.37B) and EPS ($0.99) are already above the top of the guide ($3.31B, $0.98). The stock trades at 80-90x forward earnings and fell about 7% over Oct 29-30 even as peers' demand data was good. Fortinet fell on a lowered outlook despite a beat, so an in-line-to-slightly-better Q1 may not be enough.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 revenue versus $3.37B, NGS ARR versus the $9.56B top of guide, and whether FY27 revenue ($14.1-14.2B) and EPS ($4.16-4.19) guidance is raised.

key_debates.question: How much of the growth is organic once acquisitions and the Chronosphere one-off are stripped out?

bear.text: Pro forma revenue growth was about 17% against 24% reported. FY27 NGS ARR growth is guided to 22-23% from 63%. Q4 net new ARR included a nine-figure LLM migration, and Q1 net new ARR is implied at only about $0.45B. Idira growth is guided to tick down from 21%. The 10-K warns of consumption-optimization volatility from AI-native customers.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 NGS ARR net new ex-migration (needs the size of the Chronosphere one-off), Idira revenue run-rate against about $1.5B, and Network & AI Security growth versus the low-double-digit guide.

key_debates.question: Is margin expansion real, given GAAP profitability and gross margin pressure?

bull.text: Non-GAAP operating margin rose to 29.2% in FY26 even with part-year acquisitions at lower standalone margins. FY27 is guided to 29.5%, CyberArk synergies are three to six months ahead of plan, and management says operating leverage more than offsets higher COGS. Adjusted FCF margin has been at least 38% for four years.

bear.text: GAAP gross margin fell to 70.4% from 73.4%, and non-GAAP gross margin to 74.8% in Q4. Hosting costs are guided to outgrow revenue and memory costs to persist. GAAP operating margin was 6.1% (5.0% in Q4), with $1.08B of scheduled FY27 amortization and SBC of $1.8B. My bridge puts FY27 GAAP operating margin roughly flat near 6%. The FCF margin guide (38%) is slightly below FY26's 38.4%.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 non-GAAP gross margin versus 74.8%, any hardware price-increase commentary, and the SBC and GAAP reconciliation.

key_debates.question: Is AI a tailwind for PANW or a competitive and perception risk?

bull.text: Management frames agentic AI, 'Mythos'-style vulnerability discovery and open-weight models as expanding the attack surface. Prisma AIRS passed $100M ARR in four quarters, agentic traffic on SASE is up ninefold in nine months, and the company expects consolidation toward platforms.

bear.text: The 10-K warns that frontier AI labs and hyperscalers may bundle competing security, and that market perception of AI disruption could hit the stock regardless of fundamentals. Active exploitation of PAN-OS management interfaces adds a product-security overhang.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Prisma AIRS and Idira agent-security traction, platformization count, and whether customer commentary on PAN-OS exploitation shows any churn or delayed deals.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Revenue lands near the top of the guide ($3.31-3.33B) and EPS near $0.98. NGS ARR is no better than the guide, which exposes organic softness after the Chronosphere migration fades. Non-GAAP gross margin slips, the Q1 RPO guide proves to be a sequential decline, and PAN-OS exploitation comes up on the call. A priced-for-perfection stock sells off even without a miss.

triggers: Revenue below $3.34B or EPS below $0.99 (under consensus)
NGS ARR at or below $9.56B with net new ex-migration unclear
FY27 guide unchanged while consensus drifts higher
Customer delays or churn tied to PAN-OS vulnerabilities

claim.text: Expectations risk: consensus revenue of $3.37B and EPS of $0.99 sit above the top of Q1 guidance, with the stock at 80-90x forward earnings. Peers' good results were met with selling on Oct 29, so an in-line beat of the guide may not be enough.

Product-security risk: Palo Alto confirmed active exploitation of PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces on Oct 28, with hotfixes rolling out through Oct 30, and ransomware groups were reported exploiting CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect since June. The 10-K flags product defects and a May 2026 authentication bypass, and warns of reputational harm and lost customers.

ARR quality risk: Q4 net new NGS ARR included a nine-figure LLM migration to Chronosphere, with a smaller tail in Q1. The 10-K warns that consumption-priced offerings, especially from AI-native customers, can see usage optimization and revenue volatility. Management says many Chronosphere customers are AI-native, so this risk applies to the observability business.

Gross margin risk: GAAP gross margin fell 300bp to 70.4% in FY26. The 10-K cites memory and component cost inflation and cloud hosting costs, and management expects hosting costs to outgrow revenue in FY27. Non-cancelable cloud commitments are $7.7B and step up from FY28. Fortinet's product margin fell 3.3 points on memory costs.

2030 convertible notes: $1.1B of principal is outstanding and convertible in a quarter if the stock closes at or above $280.75 on 20 of the last 30 trading days of the prior quarter. The trigger was not met in the June quarter, so the notes were not convertible in the September quarter. The stock closed at $418.78 on Oct 9, above the trigger, but one close does not show the 20-of-30-day test was met for the September quarter, and no filing confirms it. If it was met and holders convert in the December quarter, the principal would be settled in cash. Fair-value swings ($620M loss, $58M capped-call gain in FY26) make GAAP EPS and the tax rate (42.7%) hard to forecast.

Integration and dilution: headcount rose from 16,068 to 21,921 (4,223 from CyberArk), shares outstanding from 668M to 815M, and goodwill is $22.0B with $7.0B of intangibles. Two more deals (Embrace, $325M cash, closed Aug 27; Console, $500M cash, closed Sept 1) closed after year-end. Idira's FY27 growth guide (pro forma high-teens to 20%) is below FY26's 21%, and CyberArk was excluded from the FY26 internal-control assessment.

Customer and channel concentration: two distributors accounted for 30% of FY26 revenue, and one distributor was 19% of gross accounts receivable. The 10-K also shows customer financing receivables of about $1.5B net (short- plus long-term), down from about $1.7B a year earlier.

questions_for_management.question: How large was the Chronosphere LLM-customer migration in Q4 net new NGS ARR, how much more lands in Q1, and what is net new ARR excluding it?

why.text: Q4 net new ARR was nearly $1B including a 'nine-figure' benefit, while Q1 guide implies only about $0.45B net new. The ex-migration run-rate decides whether ARR momentum is intact.

questions_for_management.question: Why does the Q1 RPO guide ($20.8-20.9B) fall below the $21.2B year-end level, and how much of the FY27 RPO slowdown to 19-20% is acquisition lapping versus duration or billing-mix change?

why.text: RPO growth is guided to fall from 34% to 19-20%, and annual billing is about 30% of bookings. Management says contract durations were steady, but the sequential decline needs explaining.

questions_for_management.question: What is the FY27 gross margin trajectory (GAAP and non-GAAP)? How much of the memory cost increase can hardware pricing offset, and when do cloud hosting costs reach margin maturity?

why.text: Gross margin is not guided, hosting costs are expected to outgrow revenue and memory costs to persist, while the 29.5% operating margin guide depends on leverage elsewhere.

questions_for_management.question: What is Idira's quarterly revenue and bookings run-rate, and why is FY27 growth guided to high-teens to 20% when bookings grew faster than revenue in Q4? How much of the Q1 beat potential comes from Modern PAM upgrades?

why.text: Idira is guided to about $1.5B, a slight deceleration from 21% pro forma growth, and the Q1 guide includes no disclosed acquired-revenue split.

questions_for_management.question: What has been the customer impact of the active exploitation of PAN-OS management interfaces and GlobalProtect (including the May authentication bypass)? Are there any delayed deals, service credits or remediation costs?

why.text: Exploitation was confirmed on Oct 28 and reported through Oct 31. The 10-K warns of lost customers and reputational harm from defects.

questions_for_management.question: What are the capital allocation plans: will the $1.0B buyback authorization (expiring Dec 31, 2026) be renewed? Have any 2030 noteholders converted since Oct 1, and how will principal and any excess be settled?

why.text: No repurchases were made in Q4, $1.0B remains under a program that expires Dec 31, 2026, and the $1.1B of 2030 notes were not convertible in the September quarter but could become convertible in the December quarter if the sale price condition was met, with principal payable in cash. Fair-value noise in GAAP results continues.

questions_for_management.question: What does adjusted free cash flow add back versus GAAP-basis FCF, and why is the FY27 FCF margin guide (38%) slightly below FY26's 38.4% while operating margin expands?

why.text: Adjusted FCF of $4.41B compares with $4.11B of OCF less capex, and capex rose 78% in FY26.

data_gaps: Report date and time are unconfirmed: Finnhub lists 2026-11-12 with no time, a TIKR article (Oct 17, outside the 14-day window) cites a Yahoo estimate of about Nov 19, and no company 8-K or press release announcing the call was found.

The snapshot date of the $3.37B / $0.99 consensus is unknown, as is whether it predates the Sept 1 guide. No consensus is available for NGS ARR, RPO or gross margin. Beat/miss history is unavailable (FMP refused), and the Barchart '3 of 4' record has no beat sizes or stated basis (its $0.52 EPS does not match PANW's figures).
No options-implied move is available (no confirmed report date); only the 8-report average closing move of ±5.1%.

The size of the Chronosphere LLM migration is only bounded as 'nine-figure'. The Q3 FY26 NGS ARR dollar level was not retrieved, so Q4 net new and the ex-migration run-rate cannot be computed precisely. Year-end ARR is rounded to $9.1B, giving implied net new figures about ±$50M of uncertainty.

The company's definition of adjusted free cash flow and the reconciliation to GAAP-basis FCF ($4.41B vs $4.11B) were not found. The non-GAAP reconciliation, FY27 SBC and any gross margin guide (from the call's appendix modeling points) are not in the sources.
The GAAP operating margin bridge for FY27 (about 4-8%) and the split of the $1,081M scheduled amortization between cost of revenue and operating expenses are my estimates; the split is undisclosed.

No filing or news confirms whether the 2030 notes' sale-price condition was met in the quarter ended Sept 30, or whether any holder has converted. My conclusion rests on price datapoints older than 14 days (not cited) plus the Oct 9 close; no daily close series was available.

The Oct 30 PANW closing price and the October high (about $420) are not sourced from the last 14 days. Fortinet's Oct 29-30 price path is inconsistent across aggregator snippets (intraday -20% on Oct 29, with a rebound reported Oct 30), so the sector reaction is only approximately known.

No usable latest-quarter results from CrowdStrike, Zscaler, Check Point, Cisco or Microsoft were found, and the F5 reaction was not retrieved. Peer evidence is limited to Fortinet's Q3, Zscaler's guide and sympathy price moves.

The Q1 FY27 diluted share count in the call transcript ('37 to 44 million shares') is garbled and was not used. Whether the May 2026 authentication bypass and CVE-2026-0257 are the same flaw is unconfirmed.
No Q1 acquired-revenue split (Idira, Chronosphere, NGTS) is disclosed, so organic growth inside the 33-34% guide (my estimate: about 13%) cannot be verified.
